things.name: the Sun Insurance Office's wartime move to Wrest
things.who: the Sun Insurance Office, which bought the estate in 1939 and moved its head office staff here from Threadneedle Street in London (the end year is not confirmed)

things.name: the founding of the institute at Oxford
things.who: founded at the University of Oxford as the Institute of Agricultural Engineering, to run farm machinery trials and research

things.name: the institute's move to Askham Bryan
things.who: when the institute became a Ministry branch and was renamed the National Institute of Agricultural Engineering, in temporary quarters near York

things.name: the agricultural engineering institute at Wrest
things.who: the National Institute of Agricultural Engineering, renamed Silsoe Research Institute in 1991, which leased the estate from the state (staff moved in between June 1947 and July 1948)

things.name: the state's purchase of Wrest Park
things.who: bought by the Ministry of Works (called the Ministry of Public Building and Works in the Historic England entry) and leased to the agricultural engineering institute; 1949 is given by some sources and is unconfirmed

things.name: the opening of the gardens to the public on summer weekends
things.who: opened by the Ministry of Works, according to a written answer in the House of Commons on 1 November 1960

things.name: the institute's transfer to the Agricultural Research Council
things.who: the move from the Ministry to the Agricultural Research Council, shifting the institute towards long-term research and away from routine testing

things.name: the renaming as Silsoe Research Institute
things.who: the AFRC Institute of Engineering Research (so called since 1986) took the more manageable name Silsoe Research Institute

things.name: the BBSRC's decision to end funding
things.who: the institute's main sponsor, the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council, deciding to stop supporting it because its own research priorities had changed

things.name: the closure of Silsoe Research Institute
things.who: the institute ceasing operations at the end of March 2006 after 80 years (Wikipedia's article on Silsoe says 2007)

things.name: the driverless tractor work
things.who: begun at Reading University, whose tractor was first shown about 1958, then handed to the National Institute of Agricultural Engineering at Silsoe (the Silsoe dates are not recorded)

things.name: the camera-guided robot hoe
things.who: developed at Silsoe Research Institute by a team including Nick Tillett, Tony Hague and John Marchant

things.name: the first sale of a camera-guided Robocrop hoe
things.who: built by Garford with the Silsoe camera guidance system, after the 1996 demonstration; Tillett and Hague Technology was set up after the closure was announced in 2005

things.name: the institute's tractor and machinery testing
things.who: carried out for the Ministry and manufacturers by the institute (the World Agricultural Tractor Trials of 1930 are the start the institute's history gives)

things.name: the institute's tests of tractor safety cabs
things.who: reported by the institute in test reports from 1963 (the Bonser cab) to 1971 (the County cab) in the Museum of English Rural Life catalogue

things.name: the Agriculture (Tractor Cabs) Regulations
things.who: made by the Minister of Agriculture and the Secretary of State for Scotland, requiring approved safety cabs on tractors driven by agricultural workers

things.name: the crop drying research
things.who: begun in the Oxford institute of 1924 and followed by grass-dryer and grain-dryer testing in the 1940s and 1950s

things.name: the spray drift research
things.who: reported to the British Crop Protection Council by Paul Miller of Silsoe Research Institute (the 1999 paper is one example, not the start of the work)

things.name: the Silsoe 6 m cube wind experiment
things.who: the full-scale cube results published by Hoxey, Richards and Short; the build year of the cube is not recorded here
